name: Pekahiah
overview: Pekahiah was a male king of Israel, known as the son of Menachem. His reign is briefly noted in Scripture, identifying him primarily through his lineage and royal position. There are no additional tribal or personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Pekahiah means 'YHWH opens,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This name is listed plainly without indication that it was given directly by God, highlighting a typical Israelite royal name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Pekahiah as the son of Menachem. Additionally, it is inferred that Pekah killed Pekahiah, indicating a violent end to his reign. Beyond these, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Pekahiah's significance lies in his role as a king of Israel succeeding his father Menachem, representing a continuation of the northern kingdom's dynastic line. His assassination by Pekah marks a pivotal moment that reflects the instability and internal strife within Israel during this era. His brief mention underscores the challenges faced by Israel's monarchy before the eventual fall of the northern kingdom.
